Which of the following is the best upper bound for the length of $\overset{―}{BD},$ obtained using the triangle inequality theorem only?

(*Note: Figure not drawn to scale*)
question.worked_solution:
The triangle inequality theorem states that the length of any one side must be smaller than the sum of the other two sides.

- Applying the triangle inequality theorem to $△BAD$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BD & <BA+AD \\ BD & <4\,\text{cm}+5\,\text{cm} \\ BD & <9\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Applying the triangle inequality theorem to $△BCD$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BD & <BC+CD \\ BD & <2\,\text{cm}+7\,\text{cm} \\ BD & <9\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since in both cases $BD<9\,\text{cm}$  must be satisfied, we conclude that 

$$
BD<9\,\text{cm}.
$$
